bib.title: Chapter 8. Occupancy Tuning, Warp Efficiency, and Instruction-Level Parallelism (AI Systems Performance Engineering)

question: How do you diagnose why a CUDA kernel underuses a (Blackwell) GPU and fix it by tuning occupancy, warp efficiency and instruction-level parallelism?
contributions: Profiler-guided workflow (Nsight Systems then Nsight Compute, PyTorch profiler) for classifying a kernel as underutilized, latency bound, memory bound or compute bound
Occupancy tuning techniques (block size, register/shared-memory limits, __launch_bounds__, Occupancy API)
Warp divergence causes and fixes, with a predication example
ILP exposure by unrolling and reordering, and its trade against occupancy and registers

limits: Metrics tables (8-3) are stated illustrative; real benchmarks are in the book's GitHub repository, not in the chapter
Table 8-4 thread counts are labelled approximations, not hard limits
Chapter asserts Blackwell schedulers dual-issue two instructions per cycle (Fig 8-9); the course note 02 disputes this
Several recommendations are rules of thumb without measurements (50-75% occupancy, ILP 2-4, 5-30% warp-efficiency gains)
Inconsistent prose: launch_bounds 'e.g., 4' vs listing 8; 'Stall: Not Selected' described both as healthy and as waiting for memory slots
practices: Profile first: Nsight Systems for the timeline, then Nsight Compute on hot kernels; mark phases with NVTX ranges (Profiling and Diagnosing).
Profile representative workloads, since tiny test kernels have different stall profiles (Analyzing Warp Stall Reasons).
Classify the kernel as underutilized, latency bound, memory bound or compute bound and apply the matching fix (Table 8-2).
Read the largest portions of the stall breakdown rather than every stall reason.
Use occupancy as a means, not a goal; stop around 50%-70% and turn to ILP, locality and warp efficiency.
Validate the Occupancy Calculator's suggested block size with timing, since slightly lower occupancy can be faster.
Cap registers (-maxrregcount, __launch_bounds__) only as far as spills allow.
Make branch conditions warp-uniform, partition data, or use predication for short branches, and benchmark both versions.
Use warp shuffle intrinsics for intrawarp communication, not shared memory plus __syncthreads.
Expose 2-4 independent operations per thread by unrolling and reordering; reduce unrolling if Nsight shows 'Limited by Registers'.
Reprofile after each change and check numerics against an FP32 baseline when lowering precision (Verify and iterate).
In PyTorch prefer built-in ops, torch.where, and torch.compile; use fused AdamW (fused=True).
